![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/2dd50d4970f5c738c7cc350b8aee4668a6ec9ce4b1444698c5ecd737d01f82ea.png)

The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. Which of the following could be the graph of $y=f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that critical points of $y=f(x)$ occur when ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(x)$ does not exist. In our case, there is one critical point: 

$\,$ $x=-2$ 

Also, we have the following: 

- If ${f}^{′}(x)>0$ then $f(x)$ is increasing.

- If ${f}^{′}(x)<0$ then $f(x)$ is decreasing.

We can now summarize the information from the graph in the table below.

| $x$ | $(-\infty ,-2)$ | $-2$ | $(-2,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $-$ | $0$ | $+$ |
| $f$ | $↘$ | $\text{min}$ | $↗$ |

Let's now sketch the graph of $y=f(x):$

- First, we draw the critical point. We choose an arbitrary point on the vertical line $x=-2,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/9eae519cd7ca99aa85fe62c9fa8276a7455cbc869587296405c6a6b3caf2ee30.png)

- Next, we consider the behavior of $y=f(x)$ in the neighborhood of the critical points:

- Since $f(x)$ is decreasing $↘$ on $(-\infty ,-2)$ and increasing $↗$ on $(-2,\infty )$, the graph of $y=f(x)$ goes up to the left and the right of $x=-2.$

So, we can draw as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/1a2fd6311c5845885bfd7ed9118091a5c81c4fea8c81587db79b203a51b9e1de.png)

- Finally, by connecting and extending the existing parts with a smooth curve, we obtain a possible graph of $y=f(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/f6e473044a84d215de98e3739bea83ccaf107231ccb273c8e45db91221f05edb.png)

**Note:** The graph we obtained is not the only possible one. Any similar graph that's shifted vertically up or down could also be considered a possible $y=f(x).$
